title: Extend filter-pixel-oracle to the remaining 5 filter types (Bevel/GradientGlow/GradientBevel/ColorMatrix/Convolution)
description:
The filter-render regression guard apps/desktop/e2e/filter-pixel-oracle.spec.ts (added by task 1241) currently pixel-oracles only 3 of the 8 SWF filter types: Glow, DropShadow, Blur. NOT covered: Bevel, GradientGlow, GradientBevel, ColorMatrix/AdjustColor, Convolution.

Why this matters (regression-prevention, not speculative coverage): this codebase has already had TWO real filter defects hide behind weak/byte-presence tests -- task 1236 (ConvolutionFilter CLAMP/PRESERVE_ALPHA bits swapped) and the CRITICAL task 1238 (PlaceObject3 HasFilterList at wrong flags2 bit -> ALL filters silently dropped at runtime). The pixel-oracle is the proven guard (its counterfactual catches 1238), but the 5 uncovered types -- especially Convolution, which had a real masked bug -- remain guarded only by byte tests.

Ask: add per-filter-type cases to filter-pixel-oracle.spec.ts for the remaining 5 types, each rendering via real Ruffle and asserting a meaningful outside-bounds (or, for ColorMatrix/Convolution which may not extend beyond bounds, an inside-shape pixel-change) delta vs a no-filter control -- mirroring the existing Glow/DropShadow/Blur cases. Note ColorMatrix/Convolution alter pixels WITHIN the shape rather than producing a halo, so they may need an inside-bounds color-delta assertion instead of outside-bounds.

Acceptance: each of the 5 types has a Ruffle-render assertion that FAILS if that filter is dropped/corrupted (verifiable by the same counterfactual method used for 1241).

References: task 1241 (added the existing oracle + counterfactual method), task 1236 (ConvolutionFilter CLAMP/PRESERVE_ALPHA bits swapped), task 1238 (CRITICAL PlaceObject3 HasFilterList wrong-bit dropped all filters).

Priority: low. Effort: medium.
